checks.target: Column convention, existence, positivity and mass conservation
checks.method: For bounded measurable w, A is bounded measurable Metzler and 1^T A=0. The absolutely continuous propagator is positive and column stochastic; ||U||_1=1 and ker(1^T) is invariant. Fixed pi simplex boundary and nonnegative destruction include zero entries.

Differentiate U_A(t,u)e^{K(u-s)} in u and integrate. ||U_A(t,u)||_1=||e^{K(u-s)}||_1=1 gives tau*M_w*||H||_1; restriction to ker(1^T) and the nominal K certificate gives min(1,q_K+tau*M_w*||H||_1). All factors are ordered correctly; all starts and all allowed measurable paths are explicit.

b_H=max_j d_j(1-pi_j)=||H||_1/2 and B=A+b_H w I >= K entrywise. Positive propagator comparison yields U_A >= exp(-b_H integral(w)) exp(K tau). With alpha=exp(-b_H M_w tau), subtract alpha exp(K tau), divide by 1-alpha, and use stochasticity to obtain q_minor=1-alpha(1-q_K). Alpha=1 is the exact degenerate branch. No nominal K coefficient is directly transferred to A.

Semigroup composition on every time-translated tau block gives h(u)=q^floor(u/tau). The remaining sub-block is nonexpansive. h(0)=1 and 0^0=1 keep fresh forcing intact. Forced contraction applies to t-s, not the global clock. q=0 controls test the abstract supplied-kernel API.

checks.target: Aligned convolution and whole-cell left limits
checks.method: For delta=tau/m, each injection cell splits at its translated kernel jump. Direct finite convolution gives F_n=delta sum(h_(n-1-j) g_j). Within cell n the envelope interpolates from h_n R0+F_n to h_n R0+F_(n+1); the latter is the right left limit. At an exact block endpoint the initial term may jump down. Whole cells include both that limit and the reported right endpoint.

Integrate exp(d(delta-u)) times the positive affine basis. For x>=0 the two series coefficients are 1/(k+2) and 1/((k+1)(k+2)); for x<0 the basis weights swap and acquire exp(x). Exact d=0 gives delta/2, delta/2. The general theorem and the limited constant-c,d aligned-grid implementation are distinguished.

Every nonnegative polynomial operation is directed to the dyadic128 grid. Degree96 exp tail is bounded by x^97/97!/(1-x/98) on 0<=x<=16; both positive moment tails are smaller. Negative exp uses reversed positive reciprocal endpoints. Selected rational q is an outer bound; implemented strictness is tested on that rational. Raw lower encloses the ideal chosen-q comparison, not actual physical error.

A constant nonnegative forcing on a cell gives a scalar solution whose derivative has fixed sign even for negative d. max(left,scalar endpoint) is a valid whole-cell bound. Whole R caps therefore drive a valid scalar comparison from a valid E-left bound. Every minimum intersects same-family, same-clock, same-point or same-closed-cell bounds. Adjacent-cell output intersection preserves validity and never resets global R memory.
